notes:
Formal middleware profile -- APPLE / iPhone VTS input.

Unlike the two ho-debug-* profiles (which are pure pass-through references: zero renaming, no
curves, parameter = expression = the raw wire name), THIS file is a real middle layer: it takes
the device's ARKit shape values and SYNTHESISES the official VTubeStudio tracking parameters
from them, the way VBridger does for its VTS relay.

INPUT SIDE -- long-lived, per-device
  One row per iPhone VTS wire. The 52 shape rows RENAME the device's PascalCase wire
  (`JawOpen`) to the canonical camelCase name (`jawOpen`); the other 15 rows (head/eye pose,
  FaceFound, Hotkey, Timestamp) are not channel names, so there `parameter == expression`.
  THIS RENAME IS NOT OPTIONAL and is not a naming preference: the canonical vocabulary belongs to
  the upstream channel table (`HoFaceTrackingChannels.Names`), and the session resolves channels
  by walking the INPUT rows' `parameter`. A profile whose input parameter is `JawOpen` matches no
  channel at all, so the middle layer silently emits nothing.
  67 wires, measured (docs/PARAMETER_DEVICE_VERIFICATION.md, section 2). Do not derive wire
  names from a spelling rule -- doing that once produced 12 rows pointing at keys the phone
  never sends, and that failure mode is silent.

OUTPUT SIDE -- the controller contract
  Writes the official VTS tracking parameters we can derive (20 art axes), plus FaceFound.
  VTS's tracking list is a fixed built-in set of 98 names (33 face/mouse/audio, 26 hand,
  39 controller); the ones here are the face ones our input can actually feed.
  Explicitly NOT written: MousePositionX/Y (no mouse), Voice* and VoiceA..O (no microphone on
  this link), FaceAngry (experimental, iOS only, and no ARKit shape maps onto it).
  Also NOT written: VBridger's own custom outputs (MouthFunnel, MouthPucker, MouthShrug,
  Eye_Squint_L/R, MouthPressLipOpen, BrowInnerUp). Those are VB-private names that need a
  ParameterCreationRequest on the receiving end -- they are not VTS standard.
  Full per-parameter definitions, ranges and formula sources: docs/PARAMETER_HO.md.

WHERE THE FORMULAS CAME FROM
  Extracted mechanically from the local VBridger install, never hand-transcribed -- see
  .research/vbridger/extract_vts_formulas.ps1. Each row's notes name the preset it came from.
  Formulas are picked by PRESET, not by output name: VB's V3.0 EyeRightX is built from
  eyeLookIn_L / eyeLookOut_L and its EyeRightY adds browOuterUp_L, so the name does not
  describe the source.
  Exception: EyeLeftX/Y and EyeRightX/Y come straight from the device's own raw eye scalars,
  because the iPhone sends them and VB's synthesis reads a different axis than its name claims.

WHAT IS NOT CALIBRATED
  Shaping, not calibration. VBridger's own input-curve store is 68 rows of identity
  (0->0 / 1->1), so there is no calibration to copy from it, and its preset numbers describe
  its own channel set, not this one.
  The FaceAngle* / FacePosition* sign flips are VBridger's, transcribed structurally: the
  device axes they consume (Rotation_*, Position_*) have NOT been verified against them on
  hardware. Head position units are also uncalibrated (raw phone values pass through).
  Fix both on YOUR copy -- this file is the starting point, not the answer.

CURVES
  Every row carries an explicit curve. The vertical axis is the PARAMETER VALUE, not a
  percentage: writing 0..100 on an output row multiplies the blend-tree weight by 100.
  A row whose expression is a synthesis formula (Brows, MouthOpen, MouthSmile) has a 0.5-ish
  neutral and can leave 0..1, so its curve is deliberately wider than the nominal range.
  The device scalars are given +/-180 on BOTH layers -- a 0..1 default curve would silently
  clamp head rotation to 0/1 and look like "head pose was never wired up".
